name: Platform Observation
definition: Finds, at an interval, whether each system and each external service answers, how long it takes to answer, and the storage and the memory of the host that are in use.
rationale: A system that stops cannot report that it stopped, so a fault in a system is visible only to a system outside it. RSK-AC-006, RSK-AD-005 and RSK-AU-006 are detected by REQ-PL-017 and need this.

name: Platform Record
definition: Holds the facts about the platform: the record of each act on the outside world, the record of each call, the facts that each system reports, and the signals of quality that others give.
rationale: DEC-120 holds data about the platform here, and DEC-006 holds it apart from life state. DEC-169 puts the record of each act here. One record of each fact lets a condition that spans systems be found.

name: Cost Accounting
definition: Gives the metered cost of the current month against the limit of the cost.
rationale: REQ-PL-017 and REQ-PL-020. A limit that you find after you pass it is not a limit. DEC-165 has External Access compute the cost of each call and sum it for its own limit, gives that sum to this system. Each record of a call states the agent, so an agent that reads the records finds the cost of each agent when it is asked.

name: Outcome Measurement
definition: Gives, for each agent, the rates of the outcomes that the platform already records.
rationale: Allocated from REQ-PL-036, which answers RSK-PL-010: the platform accounts for the work of its agents (MET-028). An agent can become less good with no change that a test of the build sees, because a provider changes a model and an agent changes an agent (DEC-039). A rate that the records give needs no call that generates. This system measures and does not judge: an evaluation that needs a model is the work of an agent (DEC-164, OPN-103).

name: Escalation
definition: Raises a unit of work, or a notice to the user, when a condition over the facts that it holds is met.
rationale: A fact that a system reports is not work. A failure can be on the path of work itself, a fault that repeats would raise a unit each time, and a fault that spans systems shows only over many facts. So a condition decides when a fact becomes work, and it is decided in one place.
